outcome: Since 26 January 2024 nothing has decided the full first-order theory of the Laurent series field in either reading, or the full theory of the rational function field C(t). The in-window results touching the bullet are a partial result (an unconditional decidability result for the existential-type fragment ∃3 of F_q((t)) with a parameter for t, preprint 24 January 2026, v2 4 May 2026), a decidability result for the CM expansion of C, a structure definable in C(t) that does not decide Th(C(t)) (Scanlon, preprint 24 August 2025, v2 7 October 2026), and a counterexample to a different conjecture, the stable forking conjecture, credited to GPT-5.6 Sol (preprint 31 August 2026), which is not this problem. Sources from 2024 to 2026 still describe the full theories as open.
problem_asks: The bullet asks two yes/no decision questions about full first-order theories, with no bound or special case named in the statement. (A) Is the theory of the field of Laurent series over Z_p decidable? Z_p is the ring of p-adic integers and is not a field, so the object is not literally defined. Two readings: (A1) the Laurent series field over a finite field, F_p((t)) or F_q((t)), which is the reading the literature treats as the open problem; (A2) a Laurent series field over a characteristic zero base such as Q_p((t)), which the statement could be read to mean and which the 1965–66 Ax–Kochen–Ershov work settles. The statement names no language; the literature asks about the theory with the t-adic valuation and a constant for t, and about the pure ring language. (B) Is the theory of the field of polynomials over C decidable? Polynomials over C do not form a field, so the object is read as the rational function field C(t), the field generated by polynomials in one variable, in the language of rings. Reading C[t] as the ring of polynomials is possible but then the object is a ring rather than a field. No partial case is asked for; the question is whether the full theory is decidable.

events.what_happened: Ax and Kochen (Diophantine problems over local fields I and II, American Journal of Mathematics 87, 1965) and Ershov (1965, independently) proved that the first-order theory of the p-adic field Q_p is decidable. This is not a Laurent series field; it is the base case of the Ax–Kochen transfer to Laurent series fields.
events.delivers: Decidability of Th(Q_p) in the ring language, for the p-adic field Q_p. It does not address any Laurent series field and does not address C(t).
events.remains: Both parts of problem_asks remain as they were: it concerns neither F_p((t)) nor C(t), and it is not a Laurent series field under either reading.

checked_by.qualification: The authors of the results; the Ax–Kochen papers appeared in the American Journal of Mathematics, a refereed journal

events.direction: Yes, decidable, for Q_p. This is a positive answer for a neighbouring structure that the Ax–Kochen transfer uses, not a Laurent series field.

events.what_happened: Ax and Kochen, Diophantine problems over local fields III: decidable fields (Annals of Mathematics 83, 1966, pp. 437–456). The main application is that the theory of k((t)), with the t-adic valuation and a constant for t, is decidable whenever k has characteristic zero and decidable theory; this covers R((t)) and C((t)) and Q_p((t)). The result answers a question of R. Robinson. As stated in the Anscombe–Fehm 2026 preprint (Theorem 1.1 there) and in Kuhlmann's talk notes, the transfer is Th(k) = Th(l) implies Th(k((t)), v_t, t) = Th(l((t)), v_t, t), so decidability passes from k to k((t)). The original paper was not opened.
events.delivers: Decidability of Th(k((t)), v_t, t) for every characteristic zero field k with decidable theory. Covers Laurent series over C, R and Q_p, in the language with the valuation and a constant for t. Restrictions: characteristic zero base; the language includes the valuation and the constant t. Whether the same holds in the pure ring language without the valuation or t is not established by any source I opened.
events.remains: For A2 (characteristic zero base such as Q_p, C, R) the valued-field version is settled. For A1 (positive characteristic base such as F_p or F_q) nothing is delivered: the Ax–Kochen transfer needs characteristic zero. For B, nothing: C(t) is not a Laurent series field.

events.what_happened: Pheidas, An undecidability result for power series rings of positive characteristic (Proceedings of the AMS 99, 1987, pp. 364–366) and part II (Proceedings of the AMS 100, 1987, pp. 526–530). The existential theory of F_q((t)) in the language with a constant for t and a predicate for the positive powers of t is undecidable. Gitin restates this as undecidability of the existential theory of (F_q((t)), 0, 1, +, ·, t, P) with P the set of positive powers of t. The originals were not opened; the statement is taken from Gitin 2024 and from search summaries.
events.delivers: Existential undecidability of F_q((t)) only in an expansion by a constant for t and a predicate for the powers of t. Restriction: the expansion with the predicate for the powers of t; existential theory only.
events.remains: Problem A1 for the bare field and the full theory is untouched. The result shows that adding the predicate for the powers of t makes the existential theory undecidable, which is a different structure from the bullet's field.

events.what_happened: Kim and Roush showed that Hilbert’s tenth problem for C(t1, t2), the purely transcendental function field in two variables over C, is undecidable, i.e. the existential theory is undecidable. Dated 1992 as cited by Eisenträger (2006) and Poonen’s survey; the original paper was not located or opened.
events.delivers: Existential (Hilbert’s tenth problem) undecidability of C(t1, t2). Restriction: two variables and existential sentences only.
events.remains: Full first-order theory of C(t) in one variable is untouched; the existential one-variable case C(t) is described by the sources as open.

events.what_happened: Denef and Schoutens (2003) gave an algorithm for the existential theory of F_p((t)) in the language with the parameter t, which is conditional on resolution of singularities for schemes over fields (their Conjecture 1). Unconditionally they proved that the positive existential theory of F_p[[t]] is decidable in that language. Source: secondary citations in the Anscombe–Dittmann–Fehm and tame-fields survey arXiv 2103.14646; the 2003 paper and its venue were not opened.
events.delivers: Existential decidability of F_p((t)) with parameter t, conditional on resolution of singularities; unconditional for the positive existential fragment of F_p[[t]]. Restrictions: existential, with parameter t, and conditional.
events.remains: Full theory of F_p((t)) remains open; the existential case is conditional here, later made unconditional by Anscombe–Fehm 2016 for the language without t.

events.what_happened: Eisenträger extended the Kim–Roush theorem: Hilbert’s tenth problem for the function field K of a variety of dimension at least 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is undecidable (existential theory). Dated 2004 in the IMRN per secondary citations; the arXiv version math/0609540 carries a 2006 identifier. The original was not opened.

events.what_happened: Anscombe and Fehm, The existential theory of equicharacteristic henselian valued fields, arXiv 1501.04522 (v1 19 January 2015, v2 18 August 2015), published in Algebra & Number Theory 10 (2016) 665–683. An existential Ax–Kochen–Ershov principle: the existential theory of an equicharacteristic henselian valued field is determined by that of its residue field. As an immediate corollary, an unconditional proof of the decidability of the existential theory of F_q((t)).
events.revisions: v1 19 Jan 2015; v2 18 Aug 2015 (current in arXiv listing).
events.delivers: Unconditional decidability of the existential theory of F_q((t)). The abstract does not state the language in the abstract page I read; secondary summaries say the pure ring language without the parameter t. Restriction: existential sentences only.
events.remains: Full first-order theory of F_q((t)) (A1) is not delivered; universal and mixed fragments are not delivered by this paper; C(t) (B) is not addressed.

events.what_happened: Onay, F_p((X)) is decidable as a module over the ring of additive polynomials, arXiv 1806.03123 (submitted 8 June 2018, v2 9 October 2018). Shows the Laurent series field over F_p, seen as a module over the ring of additive polynomials over the henselization K of F_p(t), is decidable in the language of R-modules with a predicate for the valuation ring. The paper gives a recursively enumerable axiom system for K and shows the module theory is model-complete.
events.delivers: Decidability of the R-module theory of F_p((X)) in an extended module language, with R the ring of additive polynomials over K. Restriction: the structure is a module over R, not the field F_p((X)), so it does not decide the field theory.
events.remains: The full first-order field theory of F_p((X)) (A1) is untouched.
events.direction: Yes, decidable, for a different structure (the R-module structure on F_p((X))). Neighbouring structure; does not address the field-level question.

events.what_happened: Lisinski, Decidability of positive characteristic tame Hahn fields in L_t, arXiv 2108.04132 (submitted 9 August 2021; v4 27 December 2023). States that positive characteristic tame Hahn fields F((t^Γ)) containing t are decidable in L_t when F and Γ are decidable, with explicit cases F_p((t^(1/p^∞))) and F_p((t^Q)). Uses a new AKE principle for equal characteristic tame fields in L_t. The abstract does not state the case F_p((t)), where the value group is Z; I did not read the body.
events.revisions: v1 9 Aug 2021; v4 27 Dec 2023 (the page's current version). Intermediate versions not checked.
events.delivers: Decidability in L_t of tame Hahn fields with value group divisible enough to be tame, including F_p((t^(1/p^∞))) and F_p((t^Q)). Restrictions: the field must be tame; the explicit examples have divisible value groups.
events.remains: Whether F_p((t)) (value group Z) is covered is not stated on the page I read. My understanding, not verified on the page, is that tameness in positive characteristic requires a p-divisible value group, which Z is not; if that is right, F_p((t)) falls outside the theorem. Full theory of F_p((t)) in the ring language and C(t) remain open.
events.doubts: Scope: the explicit cases given are value groups that are divisible, and the abstract does not say whether F_p((t)) with value group Z is included; the later pass should check the body before counting it against A1.
events.direction: Yes, decidable in L_t, for tame Hahn fields that the abstract lists; open for the F_p((t)) case in the abstract, scope not confirmed.

events.what_happened: Benjamin Rigler, Decidability in extensions of F_p((t)), DPhil thesis, University of Oxford, deposited 21 October 2021 in ORA (the Math Genealogy entry gives 2020; a talk with this title was given at Oxford on 30 October 2014). The thesis approaches the full first-order theory of F_p((t)) by adding predicates for roots of polynomials. Its main result is conditional: if an ℵ1-saturated model satisfies a technical condition, quantifier elimination follows and with it decidability. The author notes the condition is largely mysterious. I read the ORA record through a search snippet; the thesis body was not opened.
events.revisions: Talk 30 Oct 2014 (same title, per Oxford seminar listing); thesis deposit 21 Oct 2021 (ORA record). Dated to the thesis write-up per the first-written-argument rule.
events.delivers: Conditional quantifier elimination and decidability for the full first-order theory of F_p((t)) in an expanded language with root predicates; conditional on an unproven ℵ1-saturated-model condition. Restriction: the expanded language and the condition.
events.remains: Unconditional decidability of the full theory of F_p((t)) in the ring language; the technical condition is not established by the thesis, per the search summary.

events.what_happened: Thomas Scanlon, Decidability of some complicated structures definable in C(t), arXiv 2508.17485 (v1 submitted 24 August 2025; v2 submitted 7 October 2026), final author version to appear in the Journal of Symbolic Logic. Shows, using an effective version of the André–Oort conjecture, that the theory of CM, the structure (C, +, ·, 0, 1, CM) where CM is the set of j-invariants of CM elliptic curves, is stable and decidable (Theorem 4.8 per the arXiv HTML). Per the abstract, this rules out the route through CM that Pheidas had suggested for proving Th(C(t)) undecidable. The paper states that Th(C(t)) is a longstanding open problem. v2 replaces a direct quantifier-elimination proof for CM^mod with a citation to Zilber’s work, per the arXiv comments.
events.revisions: v1 24 Aug 2025; v2 7 Oct 2026 (main change: the direct quantifier-elimination proof for CM^mod is replaced by reference to Zilber’s work; other minor changes).
events.delivers: Decidability of the expansion (C, +, ·, 0, 1, CM) by the CM j-invariant set, a structure definable in C(t) (the paper says C and CM are definable in C(t)). Restriction: a structure on C, not C(t); the decidability of Th(CM) does not transfer to Th(C(t)) by definability alone.
events.remains: The full first-order theory of C(t) (B) remains open: the result rules out one route to undecidability, not the decision itself. The Laurent series question A is not addressed by this paper.

summary: The full first-order decidability question for both readings of the bullet is still open in every source I could open or read through search. Reading A1 (F_q((t)) or F_p((t))): the best results are partial. Denef and Schoutens (2003) gave a conditional existential algorithm for F_p((t)) with parameter t; Anscombe and Fehm (2015/2016) made the existential theory unconditional for the language without t; Anscombe, Dittmann and Fehm (2022/2023) axiomatized the existential theory with t relative to the residue field under a weak resolution hypothesis; Rigler’s 2021 Oxford thesis gives conditional quantifier elimination and decidability in an expanded language; Lisinski (2021, v4 2023) decides tame Hahn fields in L_t but the abstract does not cover F_p((t)) with value group Z, and I could not confirm the scope on the page. In the window, Anscombe and Fehm (24 January 2026) prove unconditionally that the ∃3-theory of F_q((t)) with parameter t is decidable (Corollary 1.5 also gives ∃4), using resolution of singularities for threefolds; this is an unconditional partial result, not the full theory. Gitin (2024) and Pheidas (1987) give existential undecidability only for expansions by predicates for powers of t or elements of positive valuation. Negative results for the bare field are not known to me. A 2026 habilitation (HAL, unverified author) describes F_q((t)) decidability as perhaps the most important open problem in this area; the record could not confirm its author because the HAL page returned an access block. Reading A2 (Q_p((t)) or any characteristic zero base such as C or R): Ax and Kochen (1966), using Ax–Kochen–Ershov (1965) for Q_p, make Laurent series fields over characteristic zero bases with decidable theory decidable in the valued-field language with a constant t; this was settled decades ago, and that settlement is an event here, not an in-window event. Reading B (C(t)): no result decides Th(C(t)); the closest in-window result is Scanlon (v1 24 August 2025, v2 7 October 2026), which shows that the expansion of C by the CM j-invariant set is stable and decidable, and that this rules out the route through CM that Pheidas had proposed; Scanlon explicitly calls Th(C(t)) a longstanding open problem. Earlier partial results on C(t) are existential in two variables or higher-dimension varieties (Kim–Roush, 1992; Eisenträger, 2004). The AI search found one model-theory result in window, Freitag–Mutchnik (31 August 2026), which credits GPT-5.6 Sol and says the stable forking conjecture is false; it concerns a different bullet and is recorded as a neighbouring event. The OpenAI Astra announcement (August 2026) lists ten results from secondary reports, none of which I could match to model theory or to this bullet; the OpenAI page returned 403, so this rests on secondary reports. Scanlon’s acknowledgement says AI tools (Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, and Claude Fable 5.1) were used only to proofread the LaTeX and not for any mathematical research; that is involvement that does not reach ai.systems, recorded here and in the event. Close calls: whether the bullet means A1 or A2 (and whether ‘Z_p’ is a typo for F_p or for Q_p); whether the ∃3/∃4 fragments count for the bullet at all (they are fragments, not the full theory); whether Lisinski covers F_p((t)).
competing_reading: Read literally, the bullet asks about Laurent series over Z_p. If that means the p-adic setting, Ax–Kochen (1966) settled decidability decades ago in the valued-field language, and the bullet should be counted as resolved in 1966, not open. Separately, a generous reading of the 2026 Anscombe–Fehm result treats it as settling the existential fragments of F_q((t)) with parameter t, so a reader could call the question partly resolved in January 2026. A second competing reading of B: if ‘field of polynomials over C’ means C(t), the open question is one-variable Th(C(t)), and Scanlon shows only that one attack route fails; a reader who takes the CM result as evidence for decidability of C(t) overreads it, since it is a result about a definable expansion.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The intended structure in Wikipedia’s source for this bullet, and the language (valued-field with t, or pure ring). (2) The body text of Anscombe–Fehm 2026 (v2, May 2026), specifically Corollary 1.5 and any sentence on the full theory of F_q((t)). (3) The body of Lisinski 2021 (v4) for whether F_p((t)) with value group Z is covered. (4) The Scanlon JSL version and any confirmation of Theorem 4.8. (5) The Kuhlmann 2025 survey (arXiv 2512.06386) body, to see how the open problems on F_p((t)) and C(t) are stated in late 2025. (6) The OpenAI Astra list (openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics), which returned 403 here. (7) Any independent verification of Freitag–Mutchnik, which bears only on the neighbouring bullet.

events.ai_basis: This is an AI-generated result proven with the help of GPT-5.6 Sol.

judgement.why: The statement asks whether two full first-order theories are decidable: the Laurent series field over 'Z_p' (read, as the literature does, as F_p((t)), since Z_p is not a field) and C(t). No event decides either. Fragment results (existential, ∃3/∃4, universal-existential), results for expansions by extra predicates, module structures, multivariable function fields and characteristic-zero bases all answer changed questions, so they are variant; the Ax–Kochen characteristic-zero transfer is variant under the F_p reading and would be at most a case of a two-part statement under the Q_p reading, so it matters neither way. Rigler's conditional result and Scanlon's CM theorem, which only rules out one route to undecidability, are none. Freitag–Mutchnik is about the stable forking conjecture, a different bullet: variant, with AI role generated on the authors' own quote. Anscombe–Fehm 2026 (24 January 2026) falls after the snapshot.
judgement.doubts: Close call: whether the existential ∃3 fragment counts as a case of the full-theory question or as a weaker variant. I read a fragment of a theory as a weaker form of the question, so variant; under the case reading the problem would show as partial from that event. Kim–Roush and Denef–Schoutens venues were not verified.
